/-!
# Erdős Problem 273
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/273](https://www.erdosproblems.com/273)
-/

namespace Erdos273

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_273 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)} := by
  sorry

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 3$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_273.variants.three : answer(True) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℕ, ∀ i, ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)} := by
  -- TODO(Paul-Lez): find reference for this and perhaps formalize the proof?
  sorry

end Erdos273

reformulations.difference: The source uses congruence classes covering all integers, whereas Lean asks for a StrictCoveringSystem ℕ, whose principal-ideal translates are one-sided arithmetic progressions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an integer covering, replace each residue a modulo m=p−1 by its least nonnegative representative r<m. Every natural number congruent to r is then r+tm for some t∈ℕ, yielding a natural-number covering. Conversely, given a natural-number covering, let M be the product of its finitely many positive moduli. For any integer z, the natural number z mod M is covered; the corresponding integer congruence class also contains z since its modulus divides M. Both constructions preserve the numerical moduli, and equality of principal ideals generated by natural numbers is equivalent to equality of their generators in both ℕ and ℤ. Thus distinctness and all prime restrictions are preserved. The exact existence equivalence was proved for every prime cutoff k≥3 in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/273 (read through r.jina.ai, including the rendered HTML and current status)

P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), Chapter 3, pp. 24–25; https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf (scanned pages read using local OCR)
review.notes: Both declarations match the source. Page 24 of Erdős–Graham explicitly requires finite coverings with distinct moduli greater than 1 and records Selfridge’s affirmative result when p=3 is allowed. The current problem page still marks the p≥5 question open. Lean checks covered principal-ideal membership and distinctness, nonempty indexing, the smallest permitted primes, and subtraction/cast behavior. I also independently proved the exact RHS of the p≥3 variant using 12 distinct moduli dividing 360. Both that proof and the ℕ↔ℤ equivalence compile without sorryAx dependencies. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/equivalence.lean; no repository files were edited.
